summary: A Jew who shares a courtyard with a non-Jew, or with someone who does not believe in eiruv, may not carry there unless he rents that person's share. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says this is only when two Jews live there.

chunks.en: Someone who lives with a non-Jew in a courtyard,
chunks.st: One who resides with a gentile in the same courtyard,

chunks.he: אוֹ עִם מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹדֶה בָעֵרוּב,
chunks.en: or with someone who does not believe in eiruv,
chunks.st: or one who lives in the same courtyard with one who does not accept the principle of eiruv,
chunks.stMore: even though he is not a gentile, such as a Samaritan [Kuti],

chunks.he: הֲרֵי זֶה אוֹסֵר עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
chunks.en: that person makes it forbidden for him, says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this person renders it prohibited for him
chunks.stMore: to carry from his own house into the courtyard or from the courtyard into his house, unless he rents this person’s rights in the courtyard, as will be explained below.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.he: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ שְׁנֵי
chunks.en: he never forbids unless there are two
chunks.st: Actually, the gentile does not render it prohibited for one to carry, unless there are two Jews

chunks.en: Jews who would forbid each other.
chunks.st: living in the same courtyard who themselves would prohibit one another from carrying if there were no eiruv. In such a case, the presence of the gentile renders the eiruv ineffective. However, if only one Jew lives there, the gentile does not render it prohibited for him to carry in the courtyard.

summary: Rabban Gamliel tells about a Tzeduki who lived in their alleyway in Yerushalayim, and what his father told them to do so that the Tzeduki would not make the alleyway forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabban Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said:

chunks.en: there was a story with a Tzeduki
chunks.st: There was an incident involving a certain Sadducee

words.note: A Tzeduki did not believe in the teachings of the Sages.

chunks.en: who lived with us in an alleyway in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: who lived with us in the same alleyway in Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: who renounced his rights to the alleyway before Shabbat.

chunks.en: and Father said to us,
chunks.st: And Father said to us:

chunks.he: מַהֲרוּ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת כָּל הַכֵּלִים לַמָּבוֹי,
chunks.en: Hurry and take out all the things into the alleyway,
chunks.st: Hurry and take out your utensils to the alleyway
chunks.stMore: to establish possession of it,

chunks.en: before he takes out his things and makes it forbidden for you.
chunks.st: before he changes his mind and takes out
chunks.stMore: his own utensils so as to reclaim his rights, in which case he would render it prohibited for you to use the entire alleyway.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says it in a different way,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Rabban Gamliel’s father spoke to them with a different formulation,

chunks.en: Hurry and do what you need in the alleyway before
chunks.st: saying: Hurry and do whatever you must do in the alleyway
chunks.stMore: prior to Shabbat,

chunks.en: he takes out his things and makes it forbidden for you.
chunks.st: before he takes out his utensils and renders it prohibited for you to use the alleyway. In other words, you may not bring out utensils to the alleyway at all on Shabbat, as the institution of an eiruv cannot be used in the neighborhood of a Sadducee. This is because, even if he renounced his rights to the alleyway, he can always retract and reclaim them.

summary: If one person in a courtyard forgot to join the eiruv, his house may not be used for carrying, but the others' houses may. The mishnah also teaches what happens when the others give him their share, and when two people forgot.

chunks.he: אַנְשֵׁי חָצֵר שֶׁשָּׁכַח אַחַד מֵהֶן וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: If one of the people of a courtyard forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one of the residents of a courtyard forgot and did not participate in an eiruv
chunks.stMore: with the other residents before Shabbat, and on Shabbat he renounced his rights in the courtyard to the other residents,

chunks.en: his house is forbidden for bringing things in and taking things out,
chunks.st: his house is prohibited both to him, who forgot to establish an eiruv, and to them, the other residents, to bring in objects from the courtyard to his house or to take them out
chunks.stMore: from his house into the courtyard.

chunks.en: for him and for them.
chunks.st: But their houses

chunks.en: But their houses are allowed,
chunks.st: are permitted

chunks.en: for him and for them.
chunks.st: both to him and to them,
chunks.stMore: for taking objects out into the courtyard and for bringing them in.

chunks.en: If they gave him their share,
chunks.st: If they gave away their rights in the courtyard to him, i.e., if they renounced their rights in his favor,

chunks.en: he is allowed and they are forbidden.
chunks.st: he is permitted to carry from his house into the courtyard, but they are prohibited
chunks.stMore: from doing so.

chunks.en: If there were two who forgot,
chunks.st: If two
chunks.stMore: residents of the courtyard forgot to establish an eiruv, and the others renounced their rights in the courtyard in their favor,

chunks.en: they forbid each other,
chunks.st: they prohibit one another.
chunks.stMore: In this scenario, the courtyard would belong to both of them, but each individual house remains the domain of its owner. It would therefore be prohibited for each of these residents to carry into the courtyard.

chunks.en: because one person can give a share and take a share,
chunks.st: For one resident may give away and receive rights
chunks.stMore: in a domain,

chunks.he: שְׁנַיִם נוֹתְנִים רְשׁוּת וְאֵין נוֹטְלִין רְשׁוּת:
chunks.en: but two can give a share and cannot take a share.
chunks.st: whereas two residents may only give away rights in a domain, but they may not receive rights in a domain. Since they did not establish an eiruv, it is unreasonable for the other residents of the courtyard to give away their rights in the domain, as the two who are prohibited because they did not participate in the eiruv render it prohibited for each other to carry.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue when a person may give away his share in the courtyard. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah argue about someone who gave his share away and then carried out by mistake.

chunks.en: From when may we give away our share?
chunks.st: The mishna poses a general question: When may one give away rights in a domain?

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: while it is still day.
chunks.st: While it is still day,
chunks.stMore: i.e., before the onset of Shabbat;

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even after dark. Someone who gave away his share and then carried out,
chunks.st: Even after nightfall, when it is already Shabbat. The mishna cites another dispute: If one gave away his rights in his courtyard to the other residents of the courtyard, renouncing them after having forgotten to establish an eiruv with them the previous day, and then he carried something out
chunks.stMore: from his house into the courtyard –

chunks.en: whether by mistake or on purpose,
chunks.st: whether unwittingly, forgetting that he had renounced his rights, or intentionally,

chunks.en: makes it forbidden,
chunks.st: he renders carrying prohibited
chunks.stMore: for all the residents of the courtyard, for his action cancels his renunciation;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: on purpose, he makes it forbidden;
chunks.st: If he acted intentionally, he renders carrying prohibited;

chunks.en: by mistake, he does not make it forbidden.
chunks.st: but if he acted unwittingly, he does not render carrying prohibited.

summary: If a homeowner shares wine with each of his neighbors, they do not need an eiruv. If he shares wine with one and oil with another, they do need one. Rabbi Shimon says they never need one.

chunks.en: A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors,
chunks.st: If a homeowner was in partnership with his neighbors,

chunks.en: with this one in wine and with that one in wine,
chunks.st: with this one in wine and with that one in wine,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they need not establish an eiruv,
chunks.stMore: for due to their authentic partnership they are considered to be one household, and no further partnership is required.

chunks.en: With this one in wine and that one in oil,
chunks.st: If, however, he was in partnership with this one in wine and with that one in oil,

chunks.en: they need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they must establish an eiruv.
chunks.stMore: As they are not partners in the same item, they are not all considered one partnership.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: both in this case and in that one,
chunks.st: In both this case and that case,
chunks.stMore: i.e., even if he partners with his neighbors in different items,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they need not establish an eiruv.

summary: Five groups stayed for Shabbos in one big hall split into parts. Beis Shammai say each group needs its own eiruv; Beis Hillel say one is enough, unless some are in separate rooms.

chunks.en: Five groups that spent Shabbos in one big hall,
chunks.st: With regard to five groups of people who spent Shabbat in one hall [teraklin]
chunks.stMore: that was subdivided by partitions into separate rooms, each of which had a separate entrance to a courtyard that was shared with other houses,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: an eiruv is needed for each and every group.
chunks.st: An eiruv is required for each and every group,
chunks.stMore: i.e., each group must contribute separately to the eiruv of the courtyard, as each is considered a different house.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: one eiruv for all of them.
chunks.st: One eiruv suffices for all of them,
chunks.stMore: as the partitions do not render the different sections separate houses.

chunks.he: וּמוֹדִים, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמִּקְצָתָן שְׁרוּיִן בַּחֲדָרִים אוֹ בַעֲלִיּוֹת,
chunks.en: And they agree that when some of them stay in rooms or upstairs rooms,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel concede that when some of them occupy separate rooms or upper stories,

chunks.he: שֶׁהֵן צְרִיכִין עֵרוּב לְכָל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה:
chunks.en: they need an eiruv for each and every group.
chunks.st: they require a separate eiruv for each and every group, and the fact that they are in the same building does not render them one unified group.

summary: Brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own houses each need to join the eiruv, unless the eiruv is in their father's house or nobody else lives in the courtyard.

chunks.en: Brothers who are partners, who eat at
chunks.st: In the case of brothers who were eating at their father’s table

chunks.en: their father's table and sleep in their own houses,
chunks.st: and sleeping in their own houses
chunks.stMore: in the same courtyard,

chunks.en: need an eiruv for each and every one.
chunks.st: a separate contribution to the eiruv is required for each and every one
chunks.stMore: of them.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם שָׁכַח אֶחָד מֵהֶם וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: So if one of them forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: Therefore, if one of them forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: he gives up his share.
chunks.st: he must renounce his rights
chunks.stMore: in the courtyard in order to render carrying in the courtyard permitted to the rest of the courtyard’s residents.

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין עֵרוּבָן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
chunks.en: When is this? When they take their eiruv to another place.
chunks.st: When do they state this halakha? They state it when they take their eiruv elsewhere
chunks.stMore: in the courtyard, i.e., to the house of one of the other residents.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵרוּב בָּא אֶצְלָן,
chunks.en: But if the eiruv was coming to them,
chunks.st: But if the eiruv was coming to them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if it was placed in their father’s house,

chunks.en: or there are no other people living with them in the courtyard,
chunks.st: or if there are no other residents with the brothers and their father in the courtyard,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they are not required to establish an eiruv, as they are considered like a single individual living in a courtyard.

summary: Five courtyards open into each other and into an alleyway. The mishnah teaches when they may carry in the courtyards and when in the alleyway, depending on the eiruv and the shituf.

chunks.en: Five courtyards that open one
chunks.st: If five courtyards open into one another and

chunks.en: into the next, and open into an alleyway,
chunks.st: also open into an alleyway,
chunks.stMore: the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if they made an eiruv in the courtyards but did not make a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: If the residents of the courtyard established an eiruv in the courtyards and did not merge the courtyards that open into the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry in the courtyards but not in the alleyway.
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and they are prohibited to carry in the alleyway.
chunks.stMore: The eiruv they established cannot also serve as a merging of the courtyards that open into the alleyway.

chunks.en: And if they made a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: And if they merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry here and there.
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry both here, in the alleyway, and there, in the courtyards.

chunks.en: If they made an eiruv in the courtyards and a shituf in the alleyway,
chunks.st: If they established an eiruv in the courtyards and also merged the courtyards of the alleyway,

chunks.he: וְשָׁכַח אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חָצֵר וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: and one of the courtyard people forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: and one of the residents of the courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv in his courtyard, but did participate in the merging of the courtyards in the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry here and there.
chunks.st: they are permitted both here and there,
chunks.stMore: as the merging of courtyards in the alleyway serves as an effective eiruv for the courtyards as well.

chunks.en: If one of the alleyway people did not join the shituf,
chunks.st: However, if one of the residents of the alleyway forgot and did not participate in the merging of courtyards that open into the alleyway,

chunks.en: they may carry in the courtyards but not in the alleyway,
chunks.st: they are permitted to carry in the courtyards and prohibited from carrying in the alleyway,

chunks.en: because an alleyway to its courtyards is like a courtyard to its houses.
chunks.st: as the principle is: An alleyway is to its courtyards as a courtyard is to its houses.

summary: Two courtyards, one behind the other: the people of the inner one must walk through the outer one. The mishnah teaches which courtyard is allowed when one or both made an eiruv.

chunks.en: Two courtyards,
chunks.st: With regard to two courtyards,

chunks.en: one inside the other,
chunks.st: one of which was within the other,
chunks.stMore: and the outer one opened into the public domain, the following distinctions apply:

chunks.en: if the inner one made an eiruv and the outer one did not,
chunks.st: If the inner courtyard established an eiruv for itself and the outer one did not establish an eiruv,

chunks.en: the inner one is allowed and the outer one is forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in the inner one is permitted and carrying in the outer one is prohibited.

chunks.en: If the outer one did, and not the inner one,
chunks.st: If the outer courtyard established an eiruv and the inner one did not,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in both is prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as the residents of the inner courtyard pass through the outer one, and are considered to a certain extent as residents of the courtyard who did not participate in the eiruv.

chunks.en: If this one made an eiruv for itself and that one for itself,
chunks.st: If this courtyard established an eiruv for itself,
chunks.stMore: and that courtyard also established an eiruv for itself, but they did not establish a joint eiruv with one another,

chunks.en: this one is allowed by itself,
chunks.st: this one is permitted by itself,

chunks.en: and that one is allowed by itself.
chunks.st: and that one is permitted by itself,
chunks.stMore: but they may not carry from one to the other.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva forbids the outer one,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva prohibits carrying in the outer one
chunks.stMore: even in such a case,

chunks.en: because the walking through it makes it forbidden.
chunks.st: as the right of entry to the outer courtyard enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard renders it prohibited.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis disagree and say:

chunks.en: walking through does not make it forbidden.
chunks.st: The right of entry enjoyed by the residents of the inner courtyard does not render it prohibited. Since the residents of the inner courtyard do not use the outer one other than to pass through it, and they are permitted to carry in their own courtyard, they do not render it prohibited to carry in the outer courtyard.

summary: More cases of an inner and outer courtyard: what happens if one person from either courtyard forgot to join the eiruv, and when no eiruv is needed at all.

chunks.he: שָׁכַח אַחַד מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלֹא עֵרֵב,
chunks.en: If one from the outer courtyard forgot and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one resident of the outer courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: the inner one is allowed and the outer one is forbidden.
chunks.st: carrying in the inner courtyard is permitted and in the outer one is prohibited.

chunks.en: If one from the inner one did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: If one resident of the inner courtyard forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: they are both prohibited,
chunks.stMore: as the right of way enjoyed by the members of the inner courtyard through the outer courtyard renders the outer one prohibited as well.

chunks.en: If they put their eiruv in one place,
chunks.st: If the residents of both courtyards put their eiruv in one place,

chunks.en: and one person forgot,
chunks.st: and one person,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הַפְּנִימִית בֵּין מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה,
chunks.en: whether from the inner one or from the outer one,
chunks.st: whether he was from the inner courtyard or from the outer one,

chunks.en: and did not join the eiruv,
chunks.st: forgot and did not contribute to the eiruv,

chunks.en: both are forbidden.
chunks.st: they are both prohibited
chunks.stMore: for carrying within them, as the two courtyards are treated as one.

chunks.en: And if they belonged to single people,
chunks.st: And if the courtyards belonged to individuals,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if only one person lived in each courtyard,

chunks.en: they do not need to make an eiruv.
chunks.st: they are not required to establish an eiruv, as this requirement applies only to a courtyard occupied by multiple residents.
